question: How much does voice AI recover for Punctual Pros?
html:
Voice AI could recover about $1.4M a year of jobs (est.) for Punctual Pros from inbound calls that go unanswered today. Outbound renewal calls could add about $403k (est.), for a combined $1.775M (est.), roughly 8.1% of revenue (Voice AI research).

Where the value comes from

LeverAnnual value (est.)Basis
After-hours missed calls$390,000Part of the inbound recovery
Daytime and storm overflow$982,000Part of the inbound recovery
Inbound recovery subtotal$1,372,0001,343 incremental jobs × $1,024
Outbound member renewals$403,0006,000 members × 8-point lift × $840
Total$1,775,000~8.1% of ~$22M revenue

All figures come from the Voice AI research.

How the inbound figure is built

  • Call volume: About 3,502 inbound calls a month (est.). This is backed out of ~$22M revenue: 70% call-driven, a $1,024 ticket, an 85.2% answer rate and a 42% human booking rate (Voice AI research).
  • Missed share: 14.8% (est.). It blends 12% after-hours calls with 35% of those lost, and 88% daytime calls with 12% of those missed.
  • AI conversion: The AI recovers 80% of missed calls and books 45% of them.
  • Haircut: A 60% incrementality factor removes callers who would have called back anyway.
  • Market check: The model implies Punctual Pros handles about 3.5% of reactive calls in its core market (est.). It sizes that market from trade baselines of 10 HVAC, 16 plumbing and 7 electrical calls per day per 10k households (Punctual Pros demand model).

Cost and timing

  • A self-built stack runs about $0.12 a minute. Off-the-shelf tools run $1.67–$3 a call. Either is small against a $1,024 ticket (Voice AI research).
  • Timing matters now. October is the busiest HVAC month nationally (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • Off-hours calls run higher in summer: 14.1% of inbound in June, versus 9.8% in October (Punctual Pros demand model).

What could move the number

  • The missed-call share is the biggest swing factor. The model allows a range of 10% to 35% (Voice AI research). The upside case at the Invoca industry rate is truncated in the context, so it is not quoted here.
  • Punctual Pros' actual call volume, missed rate, booking rate, membership count and tickets are not public. Every input above is modelled.
  • Vendor booking rates (70% overall, 90% with open capacity) are self-reported and unaudited. Treat them as ranges.
  • The 6,000-member base and the 80% to 88% renewal lift are assumptions. Real member data would confirm or replace them.

Next actions

  • Pull 12 months of ServiceTitan call logs. Measure the actual answer, abandon and booking rates by hour and by trade, then re-run the model.
  • Confirm the membership count, the current renewal rate and the member service revenue to firm up the $403k outbound estimate.
  • Scope an after-hours and overflow pilot before winter heating demand. Track booked jobs against a held-out control period.
  • Price a self-built stack against two off-the-shelf vendors on a per-booked-job basis.
